entities.summary:
Nemesianus was a prominent Roman poet of the 3rd century CE, born in Carthage and thought to have flourished around AD 283. He was a favorite poet at the court of Emperor Carus, who ruled the Roman Empire from 282 to 283 CE.


Nemesianus' poetry has been lost to time, but his works were highly regarded in his lifetime, and he is considered one of the greatest poets of the Late Antiquity period. His poetry often explored themes of love, nature, and the human condition, and was known for its technical skill and emotional depth.


Nemesianus' legacy extends beyond his own time and place. His poetry has influenced later Roman poets, and his works have been rediscovered and studied by modern scholars. He remains an important figure in the study of Late Antiquity literature and the history of Roman poetry.
